bull.t: Recurring EDA revenue and customer expansion
bull.b: Strong recurring revenue growth and expansion through renewals and add-ons support visibility beyond a single quarter. EDA tools are embedded in customer workflows, helping Cadence retain accounts, broaden tool adoption, and build durable revenue across design programs.

bull.t: High margins and strong cash generation
bull.b: Very high operating margins demonstrate substantial software economics and pricing power, while projected operating cash flow provides resources for product investment, strategic integration, and shareholder returns. This combination supports resilience and sustained internal funding of growth.

bull.t: Broad growth across EDA, IP, and system design
bull.b: Growth across core EDA, semiconductor IP, advanced packaging, 3D IC, and PCB solutions indicates a broadening platform rather than dependence on one product category. Greater coverage of complex design flows can deepen customer integration and expand long-term wallet share.

bear.b: The marked increase in leverage leaves Cadence with less financial flexibility than in earlier years, despite strong profitability and cash generation. A higher debt burden can constrain capital allocation and make the company more sensitive to slower growth or execution setbacks.

Cadence’s outlook depends partly on the regulatory framework remaining broadly unchanged, creating a structural exposure to export-control decisions. Regulatory changes could affect customer access, licensing activity, or regional demand and therefore weaken expected growth and cash generation.

bear.t: Planned investment and hardware delivery pressure
bear.b: Cadence is deliberately increasing investment for strategic initiatives while hardware supply constraints may delay fulfillment of strong demand. Together, these factors can pressure near-term margins and defer revenue conversion, even if the spending and capacity expansion support longer-term growth.
